summary.headline: Sai Life Sciences Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR553 crore, with CRO up 26% and CDMO up 6%; management guides to a stronger H2.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR553 crore against INR496 crore a year earlier, up about 12% YoY. CRO (about 40% of revenue) grew about 26% YoY, while CDMO (about 60%) grew about 6%. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations and reiterated a stronger H2 as new capacity comes online, with the Discovery facility already commissioned and sold out and Bidar production block 1 due in H2/Q3. Management reaffirmed the mid-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin of 28-30%, and FY27 capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore.

financial_highlights.change: about +12% YoY vs INR496 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: CRO / Discovery
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 26% YoY. About 65% of customers now use integrated discovery services, mainly biotech; a pilot with a large pharma converted to a long-term high-volume discovery chemistry partnership. Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 and is already sold out.

segments.name: CDMO / CMC
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 6% YoY, described as lumpy. Portfolio is 33 active commercial molecules and 14 late-phase molecules. Three of the four commercial contracts expected this year were added in Q1; management said three are commercial supplies, primary supplier in about two of three (anecdotal).

guidance_outlook: Mid-term (3-5 year) revenue growth guidance of 15-20% reiterated; management said guidance should be viewed over a longer horizon, not quarterly.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with capacity coming on stream by end-Q2 or early Q3; management referenced a 40/60 historical H1/H2 split, with FY26 at about 48/52.
FY27 capex guidance INR1,100-1,300 crore unchanged; no FY28 capex guidance yet.
Target of about 1,150 KL capacity by FY27 reconfirmed.
Expects to convert at least two large pharma customers to integrated models in FY27.
Formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2) expected to be operational in about six months, within the current fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Discovery capacity came on stream in Q1 FY27 and is sold out, ahead of the one-to-1.5-year fill timeline management had assumed.
Bidar: two production blocks of 225 KL each (450 KL total); first block due for completion and operation in H2/Q3 FY27, on track.
First dedicated peptide development lab coming online shortly for a top-tier pharma company; GMP pilot-scale peptide facility coming online soon for clinical supply.
Commercial peptide manufacturing at a new greenfield site near Hyderabad expected to be operational in 2028; groundbreaking planned. Peptide spend to end-2028 likely below INR300 crore.
XDC Center of Excellence close to opening; ADC pilot-scale space under build.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian outsourcing demand is strengthened by geopolitical concerns and IP worries, with customers using India for diversification.

FTE (dedicated team) model: one top-tier pharma FTE relationship expanded from small scale to a sizable dedicated contract running end-to-end from discovery to commercial; another large pharma process development FTE deal expected to close by end-Q2, with work from Q3.

Pipeline sourced via three routes: biotech molecules acquired by pharma partners, molecules transferred from acquirers, and FTE-led progression. Five of six late-phase molecules added in 15 months came via large pharma FTE relationships.
Phase 3 pipeline: one customer approved in FY26, two more with regulatory milestones in FY27, one expected Q2 FY28.
Modalities: about 4-5% of revenue from new modalities, all in development and discovery, none in commercial. Peptide work is mainly early-stage discovery.
Sai works with 19 of the top 25 pharma companies. Five FDA-approved molecules in calendar 2025 involved Sai in discovery, development or commercial manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Has the shift to integrated CRDMO and big pharma FTE engagements accelerated this calendar year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still early, with relationships growing from one service at a time; FTE model started about 15 months ago and acceleration is seen mainly in scale and scope.

qa_highlights.question: Is the H2-weighted FY27 guidance due to capacity, given the historical split?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said FY26 was about 48/52 H1/H2 versus a historical 40/60, and capacity additions are behind the stronger H2 call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex threshold and what would cause a slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal hurdle rates are set above the company's ROCE/ROE targets. Capacity-addition capex can be slowed if demand slows; capability-building capex is harder to defer absent severe circumstances.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 15-20% when the pipeline is large and recent quarters slowed?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is framed over 3-5 years given lumpiness; management said it is not constraining growth and FY26 grew close to 30%, with quarterly revenue driven by delivery timing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI initiative the same as the high-throughput experimentation platform?
qa_highlights.answer: No. HTE generates more data points per experiment; the AI initiative targets non-value-added chemist and operator work, with an update expected before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commercial profile of the four new commercial contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Three of four are commercial supplies, described as decently sized by value; one is a lower-volume product. Primary supplier in about two of three, anecdotally.

risks_watch: CDMO growth of about 6% YoY and quarterly lumpiness; H2 recovery depends on Bidar block 1 and formulation start-up timelines.
Capex of INR1,100-1,300 crore is heavy; FY28 capex guidance not yet given.
Formulation entry (oral solids to Phase 2, China+1 driven) is new; management says it is not yet commercial and profitability was questioned.
Management did not disclose revenue at the individual molecule or customer level, and declined to discuss mAb strategy or fermentation capex.
Commercial peptide capacity not due until 2028.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FTE model, with a long-term framing; cautious and evasive on quarterly guidance, customer-level revenue, and capex phasing beyond FY27. Management said the quarter was in line with expectations.
key_quotes: We remain confident in our ability to sustain our longer-term revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20%, and the EBITDA range of 28% to 30%.
Generally, we don't quantify what we're doing with each customer.
